item.title: How AI is redefining the speed, cost and efficiency of application modernization initiatives
item.description:
Mainframes have provided high reliability, availability and security to organisations for several decades, across industries. In fact, many mission-critical workloads still run on these systems, and they have continued to play a critical role even in the digital world. But these core, foundational applications suffer from severe technical debt, and this introduces several challenges. Application components are not modular, maintenance is difficult, code is hard to maintain, documentation is scarce or incomplete and technical skills are hard to come by. This constrains organisations from adapting to evolving customer demands, providing business flexibility and adopting new technologies. As a result, CIOs have been actively looking to modernize these applications and integrate them into the modern technology stack.

AI is now accelerating this shift, and application modernization has become relatively easier, cheaper and faster. Enterprises could leverage AI themselves to experiment with the transformation, identify productivity and business gains and identify points of intervention. However, transitioning from experimentation to deployment at scale is an involved process and fraught with risk. Enterprises need a mature partner who can bring the required expertise to make the shift to the modern technology stack, seamless and effective.

The IBM-Wipro partnership focuses on addressing precisely this requirement for clients by combining Wipro’s expertise on domain, customer relationships, and AI-led services with IBM’s deep technical depth, AI platforms, and hybrid cloud solutions.

Shivakumar Krishnan, Global Head of Application & Platform Engineering and GTM solutioning at Wipro indicates that the Wipro-IBM partnership has already yielded multiple joint solutions related to app modernization and integration with direct client impact. It leverages Wipro’s WEGA platform, Wipro’s AI-powered platform built on Wipro Intelligence, which drives end-to-end orchestration in the app modernization process and combines it with the power of IBM watsonx. IBM and Wipro’s tools infuse generative AI through the entire application lifecycle, from automated discovery to application understanding, documentation, code refactoring and conversion, testing and fit-for-purpose deployment. He adds, “The proof lies in the outcomes. For one client, we accelerated a Java application modernization initiative and completed it in nearly one-third of the expected timeframe – demonstrating how AI-powered engineering can deliver measurable speed, efficiency, and business value at scale.”

Vishal Chahal, IBM Software Lab leader in India and Vice President of engineering development and design, further adds “a zero-touch deployment with the CI/CD pipelines around it has delivered up to 80% impact for a client”. He cautions against ill-advised deployment and integration of AI-driven app modernization as they get plugged into the wider enterprise IT environment. IBM advocates the need for a mature partner who will certify the open-source components and ensure security and compliance with enterprise standards. Vishal believes that enterprises can rent intelligence in the form of widely available AI, but none of it will be entirely effective unless it is tailored for the client. Every organisation and its process is different and therefore enterprises need customized solutions.

 In summary, generative AI accelerates the application modernization journey for organisations. The Wipro–IBM partnership enables this acceleration while addressing potential risks that infusion of generative AI may bring to the IT environment by ensuring code security, code robustness and compliance. Enterprises that are looking to retain the robust advantages of the mainframe while modernizing the applications that run on it, may have finally found a viable answer.

Visit: https://www.wipro.com/partners/ibm/

item.title: Hyring Insight Reports 10x Revenue Growth in 3 months
item.description:
Hyring’s newest workforce intelligence platform has grown 10x in revenue in just 90 days.

Hyring, the emerging AI hiring platform, which to date has run 900,000 plus AI interviews, announced that its new product, Hyring Insight, has grown tenfold over the last 90 days. The company’s quick success comes from two key product decisions: transparency and Ask AI, an aide that helps explain what employees did during the workday.

Hyring Insight is time tracking software that prides itself on transparent employee monitoring. It tracks their working hours, their activity, and the apps and websites they use, along with screenshots while the timer is running, and it uses artificial intelligence to explain where the workday went and what was achieved.

AI-Generated Timesheet Insights

A timesheet can tell managers if eight hours were worked. Hyring Insight predominantly uses AI to analyze the workday. Its Ask AI feature answers questions regarding time and activity. It holds back on making any final decisions about a person.

There are four plans for clients to choose from. Free covers up to two users with 30 days of history included. They can then choose to upgrade to the Starter plan, the Pro plan, which gives automatic AI summaries, time-lapses, and alerts, or the Enterprise plan, which is built for enterprises with 50 or more users and adds remote vs office statistics, a read-only AI connector, SSO, SCIM, an audit log, API, and a custom DPA. If a client chooses annual billing, they save up to 30%.

For paid plans, unusual activity is activity that differs from the employee’s own pattern, which may include any input that seems artificial. Each flag must be verified at the manager’s discretion, as Hyring Insight makes no recommendation.

For employees, the app includes an avatar, streaks, music, and kudos from other colleagues. No badge or streak can be earned by working overtime, and this data is never used in performance reviews.

Built to be Trusted, Sold to be Retained

The one thing that Hyring Insight never does is run when the timer is paused. The platform does not log individual keystrokes, keep track of any sensitive data like passwords or messages, or access the camera or microphone. Employees can at any time view their own data on their web portal, the same data that their managers will see.

“Our work revolves around product innovation and how much clients value the product,” says Adithyan RK, Chief Executive Officer of Hyring. “Employee monitoring software that is resented by the people who use it never gets renewed. We built Hyring Insight so that any employee can see their data exactly as their manager sees it. The transparency of it all is why teams keep it, people trust it, and that is what turned our early momentum into a viable business.”

About Hyring

Hyring is an AI hiring platform headquartered in Chennai, India, founded in 2022 by Adithyan RK and Surya N. Its products include the AI Video Interviewer, AI Resume Screener, AI Phone Screener, AI Coding Interviewer, English Proficiency Test, and their latest, Hyring Insight, which is an employee monitoring software. More information is available at hyring.com.

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System
item.description:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mad Labs founder and CEO Manju Rajashekhar opened the conference arguing that the harness around an AI model, rather than the model itself, decides what an agent can do and how safely it does it. The keynote mapped the parts of a harness, including context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops, onto jobs that operating systems already perform.

By Andrew Hoblitzell

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with Online Table Repacking and Query Planning Controls
item.description:
The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19, introducing changes to database maintenance, query planning, replication, and application development. The release focuses on reducing administrative overhead and improving performance, with new tools for reorganizing tables without downtime and controlling query plans.

By Robert Krzaczyński

item.title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets through its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
item.description:
Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos.

By Sergio De Simone

item.title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
item.description:
Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets.

By Renato Losio

item.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
item.description:
AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. Billing is the instance price plus a 9.75 percent fee; first hands-on tests report an eight-minute publish and no response streaming.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers
